instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS R1 review of WP-SCP-023 slice 023C at branch feature/wp-scp-023-023c-aggregator, HEAD commit 72f0bbb. Verify exhaustively: (1) Bypass-surface inventory: (a) Could a malicious adopter PR an opt-in-registry entry that the aggregator would accept while their wrapper actually emits adversarial content? Plan-doc invariant: schema validation + OIDC verification gates this. Argue if any bypass path remains. (b) Could a compromised aggregate job tamper with the index without the commit job catching it? The index passes through actions/upload-artifact between jobs — verify there's no opportunity for a step BETWEEN aggregate write + commit read to inject untrusted content. (c) Could the commit job's pull-requests: write + contents: write be exploited if a malicious step is inserted? CODEOWNERS coverage on output/scorecards/** + .github/** routes any tampering through review. (d) Could `gh attestation verify --signer-workflow` be bypassed if the adopter's expected_scp_workflow_ref points to a custom workflow they control? The schema's pattern enforces `jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/<...>.yml@<sha>` shape — verify the regex actually pins to the SCP repo namespace. ATTACK PATH ANALYSIS: an adopter PRs an entry with expected_scp_workflow_ref='jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<sha>' — that's the SCP reusable workflow path. Could they substitute a malicious sha? CODEOWNERS @jrnb2024 reviews the registry PR; no other adopter can land an entry. (e) Schema regex: `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/\.github/workflows/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.ya?ml@[0-9a-f]{40}$` — this allows ANY owner/repo, not just jrnb2024/standards-control-plane. Should the regex pin to the SCP source repo namespace? Argue: the schema is generic by design (the SCP repo's owner could change in the future); the actual binding is in the CODEOWNERS review of the registry PR. Acceptable, but flag if R1 wants tighter binding. (2) Workflow permissions: workflow-level is contents: read only. aggregate has contents: read + actions: read + attestations: read. commit has contents: write + pull-requests: write. Verify these are MINIMAL: (a) does aggregate need actions: read? Yes — gh run list/download against adopter repos. (b) does commit need anything beyond contents + pull-requests? No. (c) Could a step in commit be exploited to push to main directly bypassing PR review? peter-evans/create-pull-request creates a branch + PR; doesn't push to main. CODEOWNERS still gates the merge. (3) Information disclosure: aggregator stderr from gh subprocess calls is captured into row.error fields (max 500 chars per error). Could this leak adopter-side secrets? gh stderr typically doesn't carry secrets, but verify no command takes a token-bearing argument. (4) Per-emit privacy: schema validation enforces aggregator only passes through whitelisted fields; never-waiver-content invariant is intact. The error strings could theoretically include adopter PR titles via gh CLI verbose output — bounded to 500 chars + recorded in a CODEOWNERS-reviewed file. (5) Cron schedule: weekly, idempotent, can be manually triggered. No DoS surface (limited to opted-in adopters; rate-limit naturally caps). (6) Adopter-controlled inputs: opt-in-registry.yaml is the ONLY adopter-controlled surface, and CODEOWNERS gates it. The aggregator does NOT read any other adopter-controlled file. (7) yaml.safe_load is used (NOT yaml.load — RCE prevention). (8) tempfile.TemporaryDirectory cleanup is automatic. (9) subprocess.run uses arg-list (NOT shell=True). All variables are passed as separate args; no shell-injection surface. (10) Does the failure-mode handling create a covert-channel? An adopter could potentially craft an emit that produces specific failure-mode strings — but the strings are bounded to the schema's `error: maxLength 2000` constraint and are CODEOWNERS-reviewed in the resulting PR. (11) Re-run the bypass-surface inventory from plan-doc §4 threat boundaries — confirm all 3 boundaries are addressed. (12) CODEOWNERS coverage: docs/scorecards/** (registry + future markdown reports), output/scorecards/** (index), schemas/** (schemas), .github/** (workflow). All covered. NEVER recommend descoping; propose inline-fix or file as TF-023C-NNN. Output to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-023/dispatches/023C-aggregator/review-safety.json conforming to schemas/sonnet_review_result.schema.json.
